summary: Defines the Two Rate Three Color Marker, a meter for Diffserv traffic conditioners. It checks a packet stream against two separate rates and marks packets green, yellow or red depending on which limits they stay within. It is a companion to the single rate version in RFC 2697. This is an informational memo.

eli5.summary: It is like a playground slide with two speed limits. Kids going slowly get a green card, a bit faster get yellow, and too fast get red.

what is the difference between cir and pir
subtitle: A meter that colors packets green, yellow or red using a peak rate and a committed rate.

tldr.problem: A Diffserv traffic conditioner needs to enforce a peak rate separately from a committed rate, for example when policing a service at ingress.
tldr.mechanism: Two token buckets, P and C, with rates PIR and CIR and sizes PBS and CBS, are used to meter each packet. A packet is red if it exceeds the PIR, otherwise yellow or green depending on whether it exceeds the CIR.
tldr.outcome: This is an informational memo, not a standard. A service may discard red packets, forward yellow as best effort and forward green with low drop probability.

facts.label: Rate unit
facts.value: Bytes of IP packets per second

today: RFC 2698 is Informational: it does not specify an Internet standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A Meter and a Marker
sections.content:
The Two Rate Three Color Marker (trTCM) is a component of a Diffserv traffic conditioner (RFC 2475, RFC 2474). A Meter checks each packet and passes the result to a Marker, which colors the packet green, yellow or red.

The Meter works in one of two modes. In Color-Blind mode it assumes the stream is uncolored. In Color-Aware mode it assumes a preceding entity has already colored each packet. How that pre-coloring is done is DS domain specific and outside the scope of the document. A companion, RFC 2697, describes a single rate version.
sections.eli5: One part measures how fast the packets come, and another part sticks a colored label on each one.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.content:
The trTCM has a mode and four parameters: Peak Information Rate (PIR) with its Peak Burst Size (PBS), and Committed Information Rate (CIR) with its Committed Burst Size (CBS).

PIR and CIR are measured in bytes of IP packets per second, counting the IP header but not link-specific headers. The PIR must be equal to or greater than the CIR. PBS and CBS are in bytes and must be greater than 0; it is recommended that they be at least the size of the largest possible IP packet in the stream.
sections.eli5: You set two speed limits and how big a burst each limit allows.

sections.title: How Metering Works
sections.content:
Two token buckets, P and C, fill at the rates PIR and CIR, up to PBS and CBS. Both start full. When a packet of B bytes arrives in Color-Blind mode: if Tp(t)-B < 0 it is red; else if Tc(t)-B < 0 it is yellow and Tp is decremented by B; else it is green and both Tp and Tc are decremented by B.

In Color-Aware mode a packet pre-colored red is red, and one pre-colored yellow is at best yellow, with the same checks applied. An implementation need not follow this model literally.
sections.eli5: Think of two buckets of tokens. Each packet needs tokens. If there are not enough in the big bucket it is red, if not enough in the small one it is yellow, otherwise green.

sections.title: Marking and Service Example
sections.content:
The Marker sets the DS field of the packet to a codepoint. With the AF PHB (RFC 2597), the color can be coded as the drop precedence.

As an example, a service may discard all red packets because they exceeded the peak rate, forward yellow packets as best effort, and forward green packets with a low drop probability. The RFC says the trTCM has no known security concerns.
sections.eli5: The label tells the network how to treat each packet, like dropping the red ones.

items.label: Tc(t)-B < 0
items.desc: Within peak but over committed; Tp is decremented by B.

items.label: Otherwise
items.desc: Both Tp and Tc are decremented by B.
